screens.prompt: Learn the word for a guest/customer.

before.text: 客（きゃく）refers to a guest or customer. Service address commonly uses お客様.

screens.prompt: Turn 客 into respectful guest address.

after.text: お客様、こちらへどうぞ。
after.secondary: おきゃくさま、こちらへ どうぞ。

after.text: This way, please.
お客様 uses both お and 様; address a guest respectfully rather than using あなた.

audio.reading: おきゃくさま、こちらへ どうぞ。
audio.feedbackText: お客様、こちらへどうぞ。

sourceContract.purpose: Turn guest noun into respectful address

after.text: お客様、お名前とご住所をお願いします。
after.secondary: おきゃくさま、おなまえと ごじゅうしょを おねがいします。

after.text: May I have your name and address, please?

Learn each established form: お名前・お電話・お食事・お好き・お上手, but ご住所・ご両親・ご家族・ご注文・ご親切. お often accompanies native words and ご often Sino-Japanese words, with lexical exceptions. This is not a rule to add a prefix to every noun or adjective. 様 adds respectful address.

screens.prompt: Compare です with でございます.

before.text: お部屋は三階でございます。
before.secondary: おへやは さんがいでございます。

before.text: Your room is on the third floor.

でございます is the very polite service equivalent of です, identifying a room, time or floor. Compare 三階でございます (it is the third floor) with 三階にございます (it is located on the third floor). The で belongs to the copula here.
